metadata.title: ECDSA weak-nonce failure tracker: repeated/biased/related-nonce key leakage across blockchains (the 'ECDSA.fail' disclosure thread) and its tie to the PQC migration
metadata.frame: ECDSA (the signature scheme securing Bitcoin, Ethereum, and most non-PQC chains via the secp256k1 curve) leaks the PRIVATE KEY whenever the per-signature nonce k is reused, biased, or algebraically related across signatures. This is a live, recurring failure class - not a one-off - catalogued by disclosure projects (the 'ECDSA.fail' thread) and a decade of peer-reviewed blockchain scans. It matters twice: (1) it already drains real wallets today via bad randomness, and (2) it is the CLASSICAL fragility that sits UNDER the quantum 'harvest-now' threat - ECDSA is breakable by implementation error now and by a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer (Shor's) later, which is the whole case for PQC / hash-based signatures (QRL/XMSS, NIST PQC).
metadata.grade: The mathematics (reuse/bias/affine-relation -> closed-form or lattice key recovery) = FACT/theorem. The large-scale scan counts = FACT as reported per study (Brengel & Rossow RAID-2018: 647,110,920 sigs, 1,068 reused r-values, 4,433 affected keys; Biased Nonce Sense 2019: hundreds of BTC + dozens of ETH/Ripple/SSH/HTTPS keys; half-half 2023: hundreds of BTC addresses drained for years; Polynonce 2023: ~1,000 BTC/ETH addresses; affinely-related-nonces 2025; Polygon MEV nonce-collision 2026; sleep-based power side-channel 2026). Specific claims made by the 'ECDSA.fail' project itself should be treated as the PROJECT'S OWN reported findings pending primary confirmation - this block anchors on the published/peer-reviewed scans.
metadata.honest_limits: Most identified vulnerable addresses are already EMPTY - multiple entities continuously scan chains for repeated r-values and sweep funds, so 'compromised' rarely means 'currently drainable.' Nonce reuse is an IMPLEMENTATION failure (bad RNG, buggy libraries like the 'elliptic' JS malformed-input flaw, embedded/hardware weak entropy), NOT a break of ECDSA's underlying hardness - well-implemented deterministic ECDSA (RFC 6979) or EdDSA (Ed25519) closes the reuse/bias vector entirely. Conflating implementation leakage with the (separate, future) quantum break would be an error; both are reasons to migrate, for different timelines.
metadata.method: Peer-reviewed + published research: Brengel & Rossow (RAID 2018); Breitner & Heninger 'Biased Nonce Sense' (FC 2019); the 'half-half' Bitcoin nonces (IACR 2023/841); Kudelski 'Polynonce' (2023); 'Breaking ECDSA with Two Affinely Related Nonces' (IACR 2025/705); Buchanan 'ECDSA Cracking Methods' (IACR 2025/654); 'Chain Reactions' Polygon MEV nonce collisions (arXiv 2605.21498); 'Sleep Reveals the Nonce' power side-channel (arXiv 2602.01491); SlowMist 'elliptic' library analysis; RFC 6979; historical PS3 fail0verflow + 2013 Android SecureRandom incidents.

edges.notes: Bitcoin authorizes spends with ECDSA over the secp256k1 curve (Schnorr/Taproot added 2021 but ECDSA remains dominant for legacy UTXOs) - so every legacy signature's safety rests on nonce quality (fact).
edges.source: #214 ECDSA-fail tracker (Bitcoin protocol; Brengel & Rossow RAID-2018)

edges.notes: Ethereum EOAs (externally-owned accounts) sign with ECDSA/secp256k1; the same nonce-quality dependence applies chain-wide (fact).

The security of ECDSA collapses if the per-signature nonce k is (a) reused (same r -> two linear equations -> solve for private key d, closed-form), (b) biased/partially known (lattice attack on the Hidden Number Problem), or (c) affinely/recurrence-related across signatures (2023 Polynonce; 2025 two-affinely-related-nonces gives closed-form recovery from just two sigs). Not a weakness in ECC hardness - a nonce-handling failure (theorem).

Documented in the wild: Brengel & Rossow parsed 647,110,920 BTC signatures, found 1,068 reused r-values across 4,433 keys; the 2013 Android SecureRandom bug reused k and drained wallets; the 'half-half' custom implementation (nonce = half message-hash bits + half secret-key bits) let attackers empty hundreds of BTC addresses for years. Balancing fact: most such addresses are ALREADY EMPTY - continuous scanners sweep vulnerable keys (fact).

Biased Nonce Sense (2019) recovered dozens of ETH/Ripple keys alongside hundreds of BTC keys; Polynonce (2023) scan flagged ~1,000 BTC/ETH addresses; 'Chain Reactions' (2026) showed nonce collisions compromising Polygon MEV searcher bots specifically (fact per study).

The 'ECDSA.fail' thread is the ongoing public-disclosure/scanner premise: continuously catalog chains and libraries for repeated/biased/related nonces and surface affected signatures. Treated here as a living tracker anchored on the peer-reviewed scans above; the project's own headline counts are its reported findings pending primary confirmation (graded).
edges.source: #214 ECDSA-fail tracker (project premise; anchored on published scans)

edges.notes: Recurring library/implementation disclosures feed the tracker: SlowMist's 'elliptic' JS malformed-input flaw (two distinct messages -> identical k -> key leak from a single (r,s1),(r,s2) pair); Minerva (2020) timing side-channel; 'Sleep Reveals the Nonce' (2026) sleep-based power side-channel enabling partial-k lattice recovery. Implementation surface, not algebraic break (fact).

RFC 6979 derives k deterministically as HMAC(message-hash, secret-key) - the same message always yields the same k, removing dependence on external RNGs and eliminating the reuse/bias vector for correct implementations. The standard fix (fact).

EdDSA (Ed25519) derives the nonce deterministically from the private key + message by design, structurally preventing RNG-driven nonce reuse; increasingly preferred over ECDSA for new systems - though it does NOT address the quantum threat (still elliptic-curve-based) (fact).

The SEPARATE, future threat: a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer running Shor's algorithm recovers ECDSA private keys from PUBLIC keys directly (no nonce error needed) - the 'harvest-now, decrypt-later' logic for exposed on-chain pubkeys. Distinct in mechanism and timeline from nonce leakage, but the same reason to migrate signatures (fact of threat model; timing uncertain).

The PQC migration (NIST ML-DSA/SLH-DSA; hash-based signatures) is the durable answer to BOTH failure classes: it removes the nonce-handling footgun AND the quantum break. ECDSA's weak-nonce disclosures are the present-tense evidence that the signature layer is fragile even before quantum - strengthening the migration case (fact + interpretation).

The Quantum Resistant Ledger uses stateful hash-based signatures (XMSS) instead of ECDSA - positioned explicitly as post-ECDSA/post-quantum. Its thesis (ECDSA chains are structurally fragile) is bolstered by the nonce-failure record, though QRL adoption remains niche (fact of design; adoption graded).
